name: Amazon Web Services
guidance: three.ws is an AWS Partner, listed on the Software Path. Say that and nothing grander: it is a partner designation, not an endorsement, certification or tier. The AWS Marketplace integration is built and deployed, and the subscription it will open is a free front door that links an AWS account to a three.ws account and issues an x402 key. Usage is paid per call over x402, never on an AWS invoice. Never say three.ws is listed, available or live on AWS Marketplace, and never say the platform runs on or is hosted on AWS: production runs on Google Cloud and the Marketplace integration is the AWS leg. If the listing status comes up, use the product page's own words and keep it to one clause.

features.title: A free AWS subscription that issues an x402 key
features.summary: three.ws built the AWS Marketplace SaaS integration and a product page that explains it. Subscribing is a free front door: it links an AWS account to a three.ws account and issues an x402 access key that calls every /api/x402/* endpoint. Usage is then paid per call over x402, so AWS Marketplace does not meter or bill it. Registration and entitlement calls reach the AWS Marketplace APIs in us-east-1. The same x402 endpoints work today with no AWS account at all. It is for teams that want to start from the AWS side.

features.title: Engineering write-ups on the AWS Builder Center
features.summary: three.ws publishes engineering articles on the AWS Builder Center under its official organization account. The first, published 30 May 2026, walks through metering a SaaS product through AWS Marketplace with the AWS SDK for JavaScript v3: ResolveCustomer, MeterUsage, GetEntitlements and signature-verified lifecycle webhooks. It ends on bridging an AWS customer identifier into the access check that already served an x402 paywall. A second piece, published 27 June 2026, covers agents with 3D bodies and on-chain payments. Every article links the readable source in the open repository.

features.title: How the AWS Marketplace integration identifies a buyer
features.summary: The AWS Marketplace integration is open source and documented end to end. ResolveCustomer returns a license ARN and the buyer's AWS account id, and under Concurrent Agreements the license ARN, not the account id, is the per-grant identity. Lifecycle events arrive on Amazon EventBridge and are relayed to a webhook that revokes the x402 key when an agreement ends. When an end event cannot be matched to exactly one agreement, the webhook revokes nothing. The integration ships inert without credentials, so nothing can fabricate an entitlement. It is written for engineers who integrate Marketplace SaaS products.
